title: Development of Zircon Sand-Derived Zirconolite Coating to Accelerate Osseointegration on Stainless Steel Orthopedic Implants
content: Stainless steel 316L remains a primary material for orthopedic implants, yet its bioinert surface often delays or prevents stable, long-term osseointegration. This study addresses this limitation by developing an energy-efficient method to synthesize nanostructured, low-crystalline zirconolite (CaZrTi2O7) coatings from natural zircon sand. Raw zircon sand from the Brahmaputra-Jamuna riverbed was physically beneficiated and decomposed via low-temperature alkali fusion at 500°C. Following hydrometallurgical purification and acid digestion in 6M HCl, soluble precursors were co-precipitated at pH 12–12.5 and calcined at 500°C to yield single-phase zirconolite nanoparticles. XRD and TEM confirmed the formation of low-crystalline (36.7%) zirconolite nanoparticles with an average size of 10.3 nm and a lattice d-spacing of 0.288 nm, corresponding to the (221) plane. While conventional solid-state synthesis of zirconolite requires temperatures exceeding 1100°C, phase stabilization was achieved at 500°C. Stable, uniform coatings were successfully deposited on SS-316L using a dip-coating slurry. The tailored low crystallinity, nanoscale topography, and trace silica synergy of the zirconolite coatings provide a highly reactive interface that enhances protein adsorption and accelerates bone-like apatite nucleation. This cost-effective synthesis and coating strategy offers a dual benefit: it valorizes local mineral resources and provides a bioactive, structurally durable surface modification to accelerate osseointegration in metallic implants.
